chunks: My father, my brother, and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and others, may Allah have mercy on them, narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ash'ari, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), go to his Ziyarah while you are sorrowful, grieved, distressed, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty, for indeed al-Husayn was killed while he was grieved, distressed, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty. And ask him for your needs, then turn away from him, and do not take him as a permanent residence.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and emotional state for performing Ziyarah to Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Ibn Qulawayh highlights the concept of *muwāfaqa* (spiritual alignment), urging visitors to physically embody Imam al-Husayn’s state of *ghurba* (alienation) and endurance during the Battle of Karbala to deepen their emotional connection. This practice transforms the ziyarah from a mere ritual into a participatory reenactment of the Ahl al-Bayt’s sacrifice, reinforcing the shrine as a transient locus of divine encounter rather than a permanent residence.
